_README: TERM-018 / RM-N15 - the durable record of WHICH GUARDS HAVE BEEN OBSERVED RED
BEFORE GREEN. Read tests/test_term018_every_guard_can_fire.py; it is the rail
that verifies every line of this file and the reason this file cannot be a
spelling check.
THE GUARD POPULATION IN `derived_population` IS NOT LISTED HERE. It is DERIVED
by AST from the sink module named below, every run. This file only says which
of the derived guards carry an observation and which are declared debt, and the
rail asserts that partition is EXACTLY the derived set. A guard added to the
code and to neither list fails the rail BY NAME on its first run.
WHAT AN `observed` ENTRY MUST SURVIVE (all six, every run, no exceptions):
1. `predicate.file` + `predicate.scope` resolve to a real def by AST.
2. `predicate.pinned` is PRESENT in that scope's source, after comments and
docstrings are stripped and whitespace normalised.
3. `predicate.mutation` is ABSENT from that same stripped source.
4. DISCRIMINATOR: applying the mutation to the source IN MEMORY makes 2 and 3
both fail. This is what stops a pin that cannot tell the two apart.
5. every `observed_by` node id EXISTS by AST and is COLLECTED by pytest, and
its module mentions - in code, never in a docstring - a name that reaches
the pinned scope.
6. `proof.commit` is an ancestor of HEAD and its message contains
`proof.quote` verbatim. So a record cannot be added without a commit that
records a real red count.
WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT PROVE: that the recorded test is red TODAY if the guard
is reverted. Nothing static can prove that. It proves the mutation was really
performed once, on a named commit, against a named test that still exists and
is still collected, and that the exact predicate it was performed against is
still the predicate in the code.
`declared_unobserved` IS DEBT AND MAY ONLY SHRINK. The ceiling is a literal in
the rail, not in this file, so growing it is a visible test edit.

derived_population._what: The chart-health operator alert channel - lane A's channel (TERM-011).
derived_population._unit: One guard = one emit call site, keyed <relpath>::<enclosing qualname>::<alert key>::<severity>, plus the sink module's own decision functions (`emit` and the same-module functions it calls). The key/severity in the id is the audit's own unit: 'two tiers of one metric under two thresholds are two guards, because they have two predicates'. A computed key or severity reads <computed>.
derived_population._alias_resolution_is_load_bearing: api/services/bars_continuous_audit.py binds the sink as `_alerts` in a FUNCTION-LOCAL import, and its four sites include both intraday_hotset_stale tiers. A derivation matching only the literal name `chart_health_alerts` misses them. This note used to end '- tests/test_chart_health_severity_vocabulary.py does': TRUE WHEN WRITTEN, FALSE NOW, that rail was fixed to resolve aliases scope-aware and pins its population at 21 literal-severity sites.

observed.what_the_guard_decides: Whether a closed daily bar diverging from canonical raises an operator alert, and on which scale. It emitted `warn`, which is audit.py's diff scale and not an alert severity, so the row was unrankable and paged nobody while the comment above it claimed it paged someone.

Whether a wisdom job that has stopped succeeding pages. The window came from `max(last_ok, boot)` with boot set at module import, so for the one case the guard exists for - a FAILING job, whose last success predates this pod - the age it compared was POD UPTIME. 70 days of uninterrupted uptime for the monthly packet; 30 minutes even for the 900s jobs, above this pod's median life. The predicate is `_staleness_window`, which is a different function from the emit site it governs - that is why this record pins a scope rather than the call site.

predicate.pinned: if last_ok is not None: return last_ok, 2 * spec.expected_every_s
predicate.mutation: if last_ok is not None: return max(last_ok, boot), 2 * spec.expected_every_s

observed.what_the_guard_decides: Whether an alert enters the deque at all - and therefore whether it can ever reach the pager, because `emit` returns on the throttle BEFORE `_should_page_discord` runs. Keyed on the alert key alone, a warning at 0.08 swallowed the CRITICAL page at 0.20 for the same condition for ten minutes, on a five-minute cycle. Escalation is the one event a page exists for.

proof.quote: reverting the two throttle lines to their per-key form reds 2 of 8

observed.what_the_guard_decides: Whether a morning wire that never ran pages the owner. OUTSIDE the derived population on purpose: its sink is `alerts.add_alert`, not the chart-health channel. Recorded here because it is the audit's oldest CANNOT-FIRE row (CARD 27) and was fixed in this wave - the job ran at 09:05 while `expected_wire_date` rolls back before 09:30, so `expected` was YESTERDAY and `yesterday < yesterday` is False. The guard could only fire at TWO sessions stale.

proof.quote: reverting minute 35 -> 5 turns 5 of the 6 tests red

observed.what_the_guard_decides: Whether CARD 16's ratified p95 latency bar is COMPUTED at all - this is lane A's other half, TERM-012. `stale-swr` sat in COLD while the module's own docstring defined COLD as 'the user waited', so on daily reads the no-wait set emptied, a bare `if warm_ms:` with no else printed nothing, and the COLD line's p50/max was read as the p95. OUTSIDE the derived population: it is an acceptance bar in a tool, not an alert emit site.

proof.quote: putting stale-swr back into COLD turns two of them red
the second transport coupled to the primary channel (8 red)

observed.what_the_guard_decides: Whether an OPS CRITICAL reaches the second transport at all - and, load-bearingly, WITHOUT consulting the Discord channel's variables. `_should_page_discord` returns False when the webhook is blank, so a second leg that read the same fact would go silent in exactly the case spec section 6 step 4 exists for: 'With the primary channel's variable blanked, a CRITICAL still reaches the second channel' (backlog.md:586-587).

proof.quote: the second transport delivering to nobody (7 red)

observed.what_the_guard_decides: Whether the resolved recipients are actually sent to. It is the transport rather than a threshold, and - like `_page_discord` above - the derivation cannot tell those apart, so it is recorded rather than excluded by a hand-written rule.
